title: Top 3 Siemens Senseye Alternatives in 2027
summary: Compare three Siemens Senseye alternatives on data sources, deployment, human review and pricing, plus the questions to ask each vendor before you buy.
body_markdown:
## Key Points


- Start with the data source: Senseye reads data you already collect, while Tractian, Augury and AssetWatch bring their own sensors.
- Check which critical rotating assets get covered and what each alert tells a technician to do next.
- Compare cost per monitored asset, and ask what happens to hardware and data when the contract ends.


Teams comparing Siemens Senseye alternatives are usually choosing between software that reads data you already collect and a platform that brings its own sensors. Three sensor-based options stand out for that second path: Tractian, Augury and AssetWatch.


## What Is Siemens Senseye Predictive Maintenance?


Siemens Senseye is a predictive maintenance product from Siemens Digital Industries. It is built to anticipate risk, focus maintenance effort and improve asset reliability.


### How Senseye works


Senseye forecasts machine failure, prioritizes risks and shows remaining useful life, using AI combined with human expertise.


Senseye is designed to run without data science expertise or manual analysis, and it connects to existing historians, IoT platforms, databases or sensors. Sensors can be added where needed but are not mandatory to get started. Learn more about[remaining useful life](https://tractian.com/en/glossary/remaining-useful-life) .


### Notable features


Senseye uses AI to model machine and maintainer behavior, flag risks and remaining useful life, and rank priorities across a plant. It also stores maintenance knowledge (machine behavior, failure patterns and maintenance insights) in one shared platform, and works across multiple sites.


Siemens offers support for implementation, scaling and optimization. Insights start once assets are onboarded and data is connected; no typical number of days is published, so ask Siemens for a timeline.


### Pricing and availability


Siemens Senseye pricing is quote-based.[Senseye PdM on G2](https://www.g2.com/products/senseye-pdm/reviews) shows a vendor-provided price of $7.50 per month per machine asset for unlimited users, so ask Siemens whether that figure is current for your contract.


## Why Do Teams Look at Siemens Senseye Alternatives?


Teams look at alternatives when they need to decide where condition data will come from, how fast they can go live, and who supports the program. Senseye is built around data you already collect, so a plant with little sensor coverage on its critical rotating assets needs a plan for that data before the software can analyze it. Sensors can be added, so ask who supplies, installs and supports them.


Other reasons buyers give for comparing vendors include pricing by quote, the size of the integration project, and whether findings come with a named next step.

## Tractian


Best for: Plants that want sensors and software from one vendor so monitoring starts without a separate data project.


The Tractian[condition monitoring platform](https://tractian.com/en/solutions/condition-monitoring) collects vibration, ultrasound, temperature and RPM from its own sensors, so there is no historian or IoT layer to connect first. AI maps signal patterns to failure modes such as bearing wear, misalignment and unbalance.


### Notable features


The[Smart Trac Ultra](https://tractian.com/en/solutions/ultrasonic-sensor) sensor carries vibration, ultrasound, temperature and RPM in one device, the signals used for bearing, lubrication and alignment diagnosis.


[Auto Diagnosis](https://tractian.com/en/resources/videos/auto-diagnosis) benchmarks readings against historical machine data and bearing libraries, shows the evidence behind each call, and covers detection and diagnosis of 75+ specific failure modes. Alerts are ranked by failure severity and asset criticality with the root cause and next steps, and findings can become[work orders](https://tractian.com/en/solutions/work-order) in the same platform.


- **Deployment:** sensors stick on with adhesive or a drill-and-tap stud and start streaming within minutes, while CMRP and CAT-certified experts handle installation support and training on site.
- **Rated areas:** the sensors carry an IP69K rating and are[hazardous-location certified for ATEX, IECEx, and NFPA 70 Class 1, 2, and 3 (Division I)](https://tractian.com/en/solutions/sensor-specifications) .
- **Connected systems:** diagnosed findings sync to the CMMS, ERP or EAM a plant already runs, including Maximo and Oracle, through[Tractian integrations](https://tractian.com/en/solutions/integrations) .


The[Condition Monitoring 101](https://tractian.com/en/resources/videos/condition-monitoring-101) video walks through the platform end to end, and the basics of[condition monitoring](https://tractian.com/en/glossary/condition-monitoring) ,[predictive maintenance](https://tractian.com/en/glossary/predictive-maintenance) and[wireless condition monitoring sensors](https://tractian.com/en/blog/best-wireless-condition-monitoring-sensors) help frame the comparison.


### Customer results by industry


- [Plastics manufacturing](https://tractian.com/en/industry/manufacturing-maintenance-software) **:** At[Alentra](https://tractian.com/en/case-studies/alentra) , a motor that had failed once without a confirmed cause was flagged for an electrical-signature issue before it became audible. The team pulled it, the shop teardown confirmed bearing fluting, and the rebuild targeted the root cause with an insulated bearing and drive-output chokes.
- [Automotive](https://tractian.com/en/industry/automotive) **:** At a[Pirelli](https://tractian.com/en/case-studies/pirelli) tire plant, technicians check in on 98% of alerts, and the program has identified 77 failures across the asset base. One gearbox alert for possible gear wear led the team to an undetected oil leak. They corrected it, and the gearbox was intact at inspection.


### Tractian pricing compared with a software-only model


Senseye lists a per-machine software price on G2; a Tractian quote instead covers sensors and software together for the assets you choose. Tractian weighs which equipment is critical, how it can fail and how much coverage catches those failures early, and a specialist builds a custom quote around that risk.


### Questions to ask before you buy


- Can you walk me through a diagnosed fault on assets like mine, from first alert to the fix? Auto Diagnosis shows the evidence behind each call, so the reasoning is visible to your team.
- Which signals does one sensor carry for my critical rotating assets? Vibration, ultrasound, temperature and RPM come from a single Smart Trac Ultra install.
- How fast can we go live without a separate data project? Tractian supplies both the wireless sensors and the software, with expert support for installation and training.
- Will the sensors suit our washdown and classified areas? Match the IP69K rating and hazardous-location certification above to your zones.
- Which customer with similar equipment can I talk to? Start with the plastics manufacturing and automotive results above.


## Augury


**Best for:** Companies that want machine health monitoring with AI agents for operations roles.


Augury offers industrial AI agents for roles across operations, alongside its machine health monitoring. Learn more about[Augury alternatives](https://tractian.com/en/blog/augury-alternatives) .


### Notable features


Augury Machine Health provides continuous coverage across 200+ asset types in four levels of criticality. Its tiers include:


- **Machine Health Critical:** for production-critical rotating assets.
- **Hazardous:** an option for Class I and II, Division 1 and 2 environments.
- **Ultra-low RPM:** an option for assets below 20 RPM such as large gearboxes, rotary drums and kilns.
- **Lower-cost tier:** for medium-criticality machines.


Vibration analysts review Augury diagnostics, and Augury mentions integrations with other platforms. Agents notify teams of what is failing, how urgent it is and what to do.


### Pricing


Augury sets prices by quote, and the tier mix across your assets drives the total.


### Questions to ask before you buy


- Which sensors and measurement types are included for my asset list? With four coverage tiers by criticality, ask which tier each of your assets falls into.
- What does the subscription term include? Ask for a quote that separates sensors, software and analyst review.
- Which tasks do the agents run on their own, and which need a person to approve? Analysts confirm critical diagnostics, but the split between agent and analyst work is not spelled out.
- How do findings reach my maintenance system and my team? The integrations are not listed, so ask for the list.


## AssetWatch


Best for: Companies that want a condition monitoring service with human-reviewed findings.


AssetWatch combines vibration, temperature, electrical and oil analysis data in one platform, and a reliability engineer reviews findings before they reach the customer. Learn more about[AssetWatch alternatives](https://tractian.com/en/blog/assetwatch-alternatives) .


### Notable features


AssetWatch covers four monitoring types:


- **Vibration:** for mechanical wear, unbalance, misalignment and thermal anomalies.
- **Electrical monitoring:** of AC motor health.
- **Oil analysis:** for lubricant health, contamination and wear debris.
- **Temperature.**


Each account has a condition monitoring engineer, asset reliability technician and customer success manager, and each finding says what was detected, why it matters and what to do next. Install covers critical assets, machine-health data is live after install, and customers are in the U.S. and Canada.


### Pricing


AssetWatch bundles sensors and service in a single no-CapEx subscription with a $199 trial. Unlike Senseye's per-asset figure on G2, no AssetWatch price is listed publicly.


### Questions to ask before you buy


- What does the subscription cover for my plant size, and what falls outside it? Ask for the price beyond the $199 trial in writing.
- What is the response time for urgent alerts? Because each finding passes through an engineer first, ask how that step affects alert timing. In[an r/IndustrialMaintenance thread on AssetWatch vibration sensors](https://www.reddit.com/r/IndustrialMaintenance/comments/1s90y9s/assetwatch_vibration_sensors/) , a maintenance user said such sensors are far less accurate than a high-end vibration tech's equipment and typically measure a single location, so ask for accuracy evidence on your assets.
- Is there local team coverage for my site? Customers are in the U.S. and Canada, so confirm support if your plant is elsewhere.
- What happens to the data and hardware if I end the contract? The "no capital expense" subscription wording does not say who owns the sensors afterward.


## How Do You Choose Between Senseye and Its Alternatives?


Choose by data source first. If your critical assets already stream data into a historian or IoT platform, software that reads that data, such as Senseye, matches your setup. If they do not, pick a vendor whose sensors cover those assets: Tractian for wireless sensors and software from one vendor, or AssetWatch and Augury if you prefer a monitored service with analysts in the loop. Tractian also offers human review of findings when a team wants it.


Then compare pricing, support and how findings reach your maintenance team, since each option supports[condition-based maintenance](https://tractian.com/en/glossary/condition-based-maintenance) differently. Track missed faults during any trial: in[an r/IndustrialMaintenance thread on vibration analysis for condition monitoring](https://www.reddit.com/r/IndustrialMaintenance/comments/1sjtf1u/vibration_analysis_for_condition_monitoring/) , a maintenance user reported that around 50% of respondents still had failures despite vibration-based predictive maintenance.


Request the same data from each vendor: asset coverage list, install timeline, price per asset, and a reference customer with similar equipment. Run a pilot on a few rotating assets such as pumps, fans, gearboxes or motors before a plant-wide decision.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### What is Siemens Senseye used for?


Senseye is predictive maintenance software that forecasts machine failure, prioritizes risks and supports maintenance decisions across assets and sites.


### Does Siemens Senseye include sensors?


Senseye Cloud reads data a plant already has in its historians, IoT platforms or databases. A plant can add sensors, though Senseye does not require them to start.


### How much does Siemens Senseye cost?


Siemens quotes pricing on request. The vendor-provided price on G2 is $7.50 per month per machine asset. Confirm the current price with Siemens.


### What should I ask before switching from Senseye?


Ask each vendor which of your assets they cover, how long install takes, how pricing works per asset, who owns the hardware, and how findings reach your maintenance team.
